reads.title: Why these two moves
reads.body:
Both players leaving have the same problem: minutes. Calafiori has started eight of nine but the model expects about 70 minutes a game from him, and Szoboszlai has played 503 minutes all season, with recent games pointing to about 32 a game. Minutes are the input the v0 model is least sure about, but here the direction is clear.

Gabriel is the like-for-like fix. Same team, same clean-sheet chances, plus a full 90 and 9.0 defensive contributions per 90, close to the DefCon line of 10. He projects 29.9 points over GW10 to GW15, the most of any defender.

Tavernier projects 29.2 over the same six weeks, the most of any midfielder. He takes Bournemouth's corners and direct free kicks, and Bournemouth create 1.76 xG a game, third in the league. He is already in 60% of teams near your rank, so this move also closes a template gap.

The planner searched every one, two and three transfer plan. Adding Mbeumo for Schade with a -4 projects only 0.2 more, and a hit has to clear the best free plan by 2 points over the horizon before we take it. Swapping Tavernier for Mbeumo costs 0.7 points and leaves £0.8m instead of £2.1m. Rolling both transfers gives up about 14 projected points for flexibility you do not need before the international break.

reads.title: Why the captain is not the model's pick
reads.body:
Raw, the v0 model would captain Gabriel: 5.8 projected points at home to Hull against 4.7 for Haaland away at Forest. But the model is known to compress premium forwards' hauls, and our rule is to captain the premium that 70% or more of rivals captain unless the alternative projects 1.5 or more better. Gabriel is 1.1 better, so Haaland it is.

The ownership maths backs this up. In GW9, 86% of the top 10k captained Haaland, so his effective ownership there is about 187%. If you captain Gabriel and Haaland scores 12, you lose about 10 points against most of the managers you are chasing. If Haaland blanks and Gabriel hauls, you gain about 8. With the model's haul chances close (13% for Gabriel, 8% for Haaland), the downside is bigger than the upside.

Gabriel is the vice. He is the highest projected player in the eleven, and the vice only matters if Haaland does not play.

reads.title: Living without Rogers, for now
reads.body:
Rogers is in 88% of sampled top 10k teams and 85% of teams around your rank, so every Rogers return moves them and not you. That is a real risk, and it is why he is the first template player to look at in GW11.

The reason he is not in the call: over GW10 to GW15 the model projects him at 25.6 points, behind Tavernier (29.2) and Mbeumo (28.6). Our template rule says to follow the crowd when the alternative is under 2 points better over six weeks. Tavernier is 3.6 better, so the edge goes the other way this week.

His price is the catch. The feed has him at 102% of the way to a rise, so he is likely to go up to £8.2m tonight at 05:30 IST. After the call you have £2.1m in the bank, so a 10p rise does not lock him out.

reads.title: Why wait on the Free Hit
reads.body:
Your first Free Hit expires at the GW19 deadline, 1 Jan 18:30 UK. Every gameweek before then has all ten fixtures, so there is no blank to rescue, and the chip's value comes from fixtures and rotation cover.

The planner projects Free Hit gains of 3.9 to 7.1 points a week from GW10 to GW19. GW14 is the tallest bar at 7.1, but GW18 (6.3) and GW19 (6.0) are within the model's error of it, and they fall in the festive run: deadlines on 26 Dec, 29 Dec and 1 Jan, when rotation is hardest to call. Holding the chip keeps that option open.

data_room.title: The transfer search, in full
data_room.body:
## Method

The planner scores a squad by the best eleven it can field each week from GW10 to GW15, with the captain counted twice, bench points at 10% (they only count through autosubs) and each later week weighted 8% less. A plan's gain is that score minus the score of making no transfers, minus 4 for every transfer beyond your two free ones.

It tried every one and two transfer combination against the 14 best projected players in each position, then extended the best 40 two-transfer plans with a third. Only legal squads (three per club, within your £4.3m bank and selling prices) count.

## The numbers

| Plan | Gain, 6 GWs | Hit | Bank after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calafiori, Szoboszlai → Gabriel, Tavernier | +14.4 | 0 | £2.1m |
| Same plus Schade → Mbeumo | +14.7 | -4 | £0.4m |
| Calafiori, Schade → Gabriel, Tavernier | +13.8 | 0 | £1.6m |
| Calafiori, Szoboszlai → Gabriel, Mbeumo | +13.8 | 0 | £0.8m |
| King, Calafiori → Tavernier, Gabriel | +13.6 | 0 | £0.9m |

## Alternatives considered

The -4 plan is the top raw number, but it beats the best free plan by only 0.2, well under the 2 point margin a hit has to clear. Selling Schade instead of Szoboszlai projects 0.6 less: Schade expects about 65 minutes a game, Szoboszlai about 32.

## How confident we are

Fairly. The gain comes mostly from minutes: Szoboszlai expects the fewest minutes in your squad (32) and Calafiori the third fewest (70), and both replacements expect 90. Minutes are the model's weakest input, but the gap here is large. Fixture and price assumptions move the gain by about a point either way. The model cannot see transfers you have already made for GW10, so check the squad before you confirm.

data_room.title: When to play your first Free Hit
data_room.intro: Your first Free Hit expires at the GW19 deadline (1 Jan, 18:30 UK). There are no blank gameweeks before then, so its value comes from fixtures and rotation.
data_room.bottom_line: Play it in GW18 or GW19. Decide on 26 Dec, with real team news.
data_room.body:
## Why not GW14, the tallest bar

GW14 leads GW18 by 0.8 points, which is less than this model can tell apart. Playing it early also leaves nothing in hand for the festive run, when GW17, GW18 and GW19 land within seven days (deadlines 26 Dec, 29 Dec and 1 Jan).

## How this was worked out

For each gameweek, the planner builds the best eleven your £101.1m budget allows, keeping £16.5m back for a cheap bench, and compares it with the best eleven from your current squad. The captain counts double in both. Projections come from the v0 model.
data_room.confidence: Not very, and that is why the call is to wait. The v0 model has no rotation model yet, which matters most in the festive weeks. Treat any gap under 1 point as a tie. Play it early only if three or more starters are out in the same week.
